example_prompt: Accept a Flutterwave chargeback, or decline it with proof of delivery, before its due date.

id.description: Path parameter. ID of the chargeback

status.description: The status indicates the final resolution of a dispute or request, showing whether it has been accepted or declined.

due_datetime.description: The due_datetime specifies the exact date and time by which an action or response is required. This is typically used to set deadlines for submitting documentation or responding to a chargeback.

proof_data.description: Base64 encoded string of proof against chargeback

charge_id.description: ID of the charge tied to this chargeback

stage.description: The stage describes the current phase of a chargeback dispute

status.description: The status field tracks the current state or outcome of a chargeback dispute, providing a comprehensive overview of its lifecycle.

type.description: The type categorizes the chargeback based on whether it originates from a transaction within the same country (local) or across different countries (international).

due_datetime.description: The due_datetime specifies the exact date and time by which an action or response is required. This is typically used to set deadlines for submitting documentation or responding to a chargeback.

created_datetime.description: The created_datetime indicates the exact date and time when the chargeback record was initially created in the system. This timestamp helps in tracking the age of the dispute.

updated_datetime.description: The updated_datetime specifies the most recent date and time when any information related to the chargeback record was modified or updated. This helps in tracking the last activity on the dispute.

settlement_id.description: ID of the settlement tied to this chargeback

message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 1700404 CHARGEBACK_NOT_FOUND, 1703400 CHARGEBACK_DECLINE_INVALID, 1704400 CHARGEBACK_PROOF_INVALID, 1705500 CHARGEBACK_PROOF_UPLOAD_FAILED, 1706400 CHARGEBACK_DUE_DATE_INVALID (deadline passed), 1707400 CHARGEBACK_AMOUNT_INVALID.

gotchas: Auth (OAuth2 client credentials): POST grant_type=client_credentials, client_id and client_secret as application/x-www-form-urlencoded to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token (same token URL for sandbox and production), then send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Docs (Authentication): "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. FLUTTERWAVE_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS = base64(client_id:client_secret) is an afrotools convention, decoded locally; Flutterwave never receives it. Sandbox base URL: https://developersandbox-api.flutterwave.com ("We archive your test data after 30 days.")

Headers: X-Trace-Id is optional on this PUT (the headers guide lists it under 'Optional API Headers'; "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters.", 12-255 characters). The API reference documents no X-Idempotency-Key for this endpoint.
status you can set: accepted, declined, partially-accepted. won / lost / reversed are set by Flutterwave.

Decline: Docs (Chargebacks): "with the `status` set to `declined` and the link to the evidence passed as `uploaded_proof`." The error table adds that declined chargebacks must have a comment and proof (1703400). proof_data (base64) is the documented alternative to the uploaded_proof link.
Open question: partially-accepted and the amount field are in the API reference only; the guide doesn't describe them, and the response's status enum doesn't list partially-accepted.
Answer before data.due_datetime (48 hours): after it, 1706400 CHARGEBACK_DUE_DATE_INVALID.

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 1700404 CHARGEBACK_NOT_FOUND, 1703400 CHARGEBACK_DECLINE_INVALID, 1704400 CHARGEBACK_PROOF_INVALID, 1705500 CHARGEBACK_PROOF_UPLOAD_FAILED, 1706400 CHARGEBACK_DUE_DATE_INVALID (deadline passed), 1707400 CHARGEBACK_AMOUNT_INVALID. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
